rounds.text: The valuation of QMS Medical Allied Services Ltd rests on expectations that the underlying financials do not support, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 153 per share against a market price of Rs 171, creating a negative margin of safety of -11.8% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current share price demands an 11.5% earnings growth rate, which exceeds the 10.0% assumed in the base case [E37]. This disconnect is compounded by a cyclical earnings profile and a price-led signal where recent price growth outpaces profit growth by 85%, showing that market expectations are running well ahead of actual delivery [E47, E48]. Fundamental headwinds further challenge the valuation, notably a compounded profit growth of -15% over the trailing twelve months and a low return on equity of 10% to 12% [E15, E18, E19, E51]. Operational risk is also visible in rising borrowings, which increased to Rs 74 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 60 Cr a year prior, alongside a promoter group that has reduced its holding by 5.56 percentage points since December 2022 [E29, E31, E52]. Conceded: the company demonstrates solid cash conversion of 1.58x and generated Rs 19 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E24, E26].

Conceded: [E35, E36, E37, E47] DCF intrinsic value stands at Rs 153 against a market price of Rs 171, and price growth has recently outpaced profit growth [E35, E36, E37, E47]. However, the bear's narrow focus on model outputs ignores the overwhelming confirmation from the quantitative rule-based screen, which awards the stock a strong overall score of 86 out of 100 [E53]. Furthermore, the company's fundamental delivery shines through stellar year-on-year metrics, including a 22% surge in sales and a 25% leap in net profit [E54, E56]. Conceded: [E15, E51] trailing profit growth is negative and long-term ROE has been low [E15, E51], but cash generation completely offsets these concerns with operating cash flow hitting Rs 19 Cr and perfect cash conversion of 1.58x, fully backing profits with actual cash [E24, E25]. Conceded: [E29, E52] borrowings rose and promoter holdings decreased [E29, E52], yet institutional backing is actively expanding, evidenced by domestic institutions growing their stake and a positive institutional money flow signal [E33, E34]. Finally, the business operates directly within a powerful healthcare sector tailwind scored at +0.77, providing a supportive macro backdrop that underpins its ongoing market momentum [E58].

Conceded: [E53, E54, E56] the rules-based screen score is 86 out of 100 with 22% sales growth and 25% net profit growth. However, those backward-looking metrics collide with a trailing twelve-month profit contraction of -15% [E15] and an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend [E22]. While the bull points to strong cash flow [E24, E25], borrowings expanded from Rs 60 Cr to Rs 74 Cr over the same period [E29]. Conceded: [E33, E34] domestic institutions increased their stake to 1.30% with positive money flow, but overall promoter holding has persistently declined by 5.56 percentage points down to 68.11% [E31, E52]. The reliance on sector tailwinds [E58] ignores that the company's P/B of 3.28x exceeds sector benchmarks [E7] while posting a low 3-year median ROE of 12.0% [E51]. Finally, price growth exceeding profit growth by 85% [E47] underscores that expectations are running well ahead of actual delivery alongside a negative margin of safety [E36].

Conceded: [E15] trailing twelve-month profit growth sits at -15% and [E22] the yearly operating-margin trend is inconsistent. However, that backward-looking volatility obscures a pristine cash generation profile where Mar 2026 operating and free cash flows both hit Rs 19 Cr with a cash conversion of 1.58x, meaning profits are fully backed by hard cash [E24, E25, E26]. Conceded: [E29] borrowings expanded to Rs 74 Cr, yet this moderate leverage sits against a healthy dividend payout of 56.4% [E27, E49]. Conceded: [E31] promoter holding declined to 68.11%, but domestic institutions established a positive footprint with their stake rising to 1.30% alongside positive institutional money flow [E33, E34]. Conceded: [E51] the 3-year median ROE is 12%, but the company's ROCE of 12.91% outpaces the sector benchmark of 11.89% and sector median of 12.6% [E10, E63]. Finally, the stock boasts a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 while trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40, E41].

Conceded: [E24, E25, E26] operating and free cash flows hit Rs 19 Cr with a 1.58x conversion in Mar 2026. However, that strong cash snapshot clashes directly with a contracting business reality where trailing twelve-month profit growth has plummeted by -15% and yearly margins remain inconsistent [E15, E22]. Conceded: [E10] ROCE outpaces the sector benchmark, yet the company's 3-year median ROE languishes at a low 12% and single-year ROE drops further to 10%, highlighting persistent inefficiency in generating returns for shareholders [E13, E18, E51]. Conceded: [E33, E34] domestic institutions increased their holding alongside positive money flow, but overall promoter ownership has suffered a steady dilution down to 68.11% from 73.67% [E31]. Conceded: [E40, E41] relative strength sits at a maximum 100 with the price above key moving averages, but this momentum is completely disconnected from fundamentals as price growth outpaces profit growth by 85% [E47]. Finally, expanding borrowings to Rs 74 Cr while maintaining high dividend payouts undercuts the stability of those cash flows [E29, E49].
